title: Iman Gadzhi on stacking skills, monk mode cycles, and why environment shapes success
summary: Iman Gadzhi explains how he stacked self-education, health, social skills and wealth in order, runs 6 months of monk mode followed by months of play, and why he teaches agencies as the lowest-risk path to 10k a month. He also covers hiring and profit share, trauma, and why money alone doesn't fix insecurity.

principles.text: Stack skills in an order that compounds; ask if a skill still pays off if the current business disappears.
principles.quote: let's say if that business goes away, is that something that's will still you know um give me dividends for decades to come.

principles.text: Immerse intensely in a habit, then back out and integrate it sustainably.
principles.quote: I get really immersed in it and then I sort of try to integrate.

principles.text: Service-based agencies are the best route to 10k a month because failure costs almost nothing.
principles.quote: you can fall flat on your ass for four months, never sign a client, have no success and it's not costing you anything

principles.text: Most success comes from basics: no drinking, no weed, nine hours of sleep. Information is abundant; digesting and implementing it is the difference.
principles.quote: honestly 70% of success is just stop drinking, stop smoking weed.

principles.text: Know your own seasonality and work with it: 6 months hyper-focused, then a lighter stretch.
principles.quote: the first 6 months a year I'm the hardest working on the team. And for 3 months a year I'm the least hard working on the team.

principles.text: Once you scale, hiring and culture matter most; give long-tenured staff profit share so they are as incentivized as you.
principles.quote: I realized really the most important thing once you get to a certain stage is is hiring and and you know, maintaining a good company culture
